title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 545-547, cote 140-3, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'). Grothendieck studies how elements u of a Galois/Teichmüller-type group (Gal(Q̄/Q) or its combinatorial substitute, close to what is now called the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group) act on the profinite modular group SL(2,Z)^ = π̂1 of M_{1,1}. The 'loop equation' encodes the relations ρ^3 = σ^2 = ±1 for the standard generators. He works mainly in M~_{0,3}[0]. The previous page says this was technically the most elegant setting, adopted from §45.

On the previous page he defines two maps: u ↦ a, into T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1, and u ↦ b, into N'_σ(Ẑ)/±1. T_ρ is the centraliser torus of the order-3/6 element ρ. N'_σ is (a variant of) the normaliser of the torus attached to the order-4 element σ. In modern terms, u sends ρ to a conjugate of a χ(u)-power of ρ. The conjugating element, read in the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ), is defined only modulo the centraliser of ρ. This gives a class with values in the Ẑ-points of the CM torus attached to Z[j] (j = e^{2πi/3}). Likewise for σ, with the torus attached to Z[i], and its normaliser because of the inversion. This page opens by fixing the normalisation: the maps are chosen so that they are trivial on L_0^{Π̂} (a reference subgroup, notation unclear).

The rest of the page is a historical and programmatic note:
- The quantities a, b emerged gradually in the computations from §44 (p. 366' ff).
- Their role began to be understood only from §48 III-V.
- A complete understanding of their nature, and of the schemes/groups involved, came only in the last (two?) days, and remains fragile.

He then lists directions for deeper study:
(a) Make explicit the meaning of a, b in terms of the class fields of Q(j) and Q(i). The second field is most likely Q(i), overwritten. These are the CM fields of the two elliptic points j = 0 and j = 1728 of M_{1,1}. Indeed, under the congruence quotient the Galois action at these points is the Galois action on torsion of the CM curves y² = x³ − 1 and y² = x³ − x, described by CM class field theory (Hecke characters / Shimura reciprocity). So a, b should be the idelic Galois characters of those CM curves.
(b) Make explicit the meaning of the results via the theory of 'congruence' maps (cartes 'congruentielles'). These are dessins/maps whose monodromy factors through the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ)' of SL(2,Z)^'.

The next page continues with (c) arithmetic structure on M_{g,ν} linked to class field theory, (d) the extra compatibility conditions of §47 on α, β, and (e) systematisation beyond SL2.

Mathematically, the page states no theorem. It records the identification of the 'loop-equation parameters' attached to the order-3 and order-2 elliptic points with CM-torus-valued invariants, and proposes interpreting them through class field theory of Q(j), Q(i) and congruence dessins.
errors: No mathematical claims are proved on this page, so there is nothing to check for correctness. The description of a, b as living in T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1 and N'_σ(Ẑ)/±1 is consistent with the expected structure: centraliser and normaliser of CM tori in SL2(Ẑ). Grothendieck himself flags his understanding as 'fragile'.

ideas.what: Parameters a, b attached to the action of an element u on the elliptic generators ρ (order 3) and σ (order 4) of SL(2,Z)^, valued in Ẑ-points of the centraliser torus T_ρ and the torus normaliser N'_σ (mod ±1), normalised to be trivial on a reference subgroup
ideas.modern_name: Cocycles/characters attached to the decomposition groups at the elliptic points j = 0, 1728 of M_{1,1}; Galois action at CM tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (Galois action on π1 of once-punctured elliptic curves / M_{1,1}, 1990s); Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps (1997, GT and M_{1,1} with order-4 and order-6 torsion); Hain-Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions SL2(Z), GT and the Teichmüller tower in general terms, but not these parameters

ideas.what: Programme to interpret a, b through class field theory of Q(j) and Q(i), the CM fields of the elliptic points
ideas.modern_name: CM main theorem / Hecke characters of y² = x³ − 1 and y² = x³ − x, viewed as restriction of the outer Galois representation on π̂1(M_{1,1}) to elliptic decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring, Shimura-Taniyama (CM theory); the link to π̂1(M_{1,1}) is implicit in Nakamura's and Hain-Matsumoto's work

ideas.what: Interpreting the results via 'congruence' maps: dessins whose monodromy factors through the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ)' of SL(2,Z)^'
ideas.modern_name: Congruence dessins / congruence subgroups of the modular group and their Galois action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical modular-curve theory; for dessins, e.g. work of Shabat, Birch, Jones and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses dessins and SL2(Z) but not congruence maps in this sense

ideas.what: Chronology: a, b appear from §44 (p. 366'), are clarified in §48 III-V, and the groups involved are understood only in the last days
ideas.modern_name: Historical/dating information on the Longue Marche follow-up

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly ties the invariants of his 'loop equation' (action on π̂1 of M_{1,1}) at the order-3 and order-4 elliptic generators to class field theory of Q(j) and Q(i). In effect, the GT-type parameters restricted to elliptic points should be the CM Hecke characters of the curves with j = 0, 1728. He also wants to read the results through congruence dessins.
missed.quote: a) Expliciter la signification ... des corps de classes de Q(j) et de Q(i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Later literature (Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps, Nakamura, Hain-Matsumoto) studies GT-type groups for M_{1,1} and Galois action at tangential base points. However, an explicit formulation of GT-parameters at elliptic points as idelic CM characters valued in T(Ẑ), N(Ẑ) is not standard. It would give a concrete arithmetic check on GT vs Gal(Q̄/Q).

missed.claim: The programme (a)-(b) is left open, and Grothendieck admits the understanding is fragile.
missed.quote: Cette compréhension reste d'ailleurs pour le moment assez fragile, et il faudrait approfondir dans plusieurs directions
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Explicit 'congruence' dessin interpretations of the GT action on SL2(Z)^ remain sparse. This is a concrete open thread.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a retrospective and programmatic page. The link between elliptic-point parameters and CM class field theory of Q(j), Q(i) is natural to experts, since Galois acts on CM torsion via the CM characters. Still, seeing Grothendieck formulate it explicitly within his GT-like 'loop equation' framework for SL2(Z)^ is a notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'de Q(j) et {+de+} Q(j')' should most likely read 'de Q(j) et de Q(i)' (the second letter is overwritten). j and i are the cube and fourth roots of unity, the CM fields of the elliptic points ρ, σ.
'cartes "anguline"' should most likely read 'cartes "congruentielles"', consistent with the parenthesis about quotients SL(2,Ẑ)' of SL(2,Z)^'.
'des prin-cipes des schémas ou groupes' is probably 'des principaux schémas ou groupes'.
'en ces [-...-] derniers jours' is probably 'en ces deux derniers jours'.
'(i.e. ... subordonnées à des repr.' is probably '(i.e. correspondant à des repr. quotients SL(2,Ẑ)' de SL(2,Z)^')'.
